intent: To illustrate how store psychology influences a large proportion of purchases at IKEA to be unplanned.

units.meaning: The estimated share of IKEA purchases that are unplanned is 58.3%, shown as the yellow pie slice.
accepted_routes: more than half of purchases are unplanned
units.visual_evidence_rule: The yellow pie slice must be visible and labeled or annotated as 58.3% / approximately 58%.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'items purchased at Ikea are unplanned' clause
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state the unplanned share as 58.3% rather than the narration's 60%?

units.meaning: The complementary planned share is 41.7%, so unplanned plus planned makes 100%.

basis.note: used to derive the complementary total

units.visual_evidence_rule: The white pie slice must be visible and labeled or annotated as 41.7% / approximately 42%.
units.temporal_anchor: optional; after the unplanned clause if the planned complement is shown
units.reviewer_question: Is the 41.7% planned complement required, or merely useful context?

units.meaning: Unplanned purchases exceed planned purchases by 16.6 percentage points.
accepted_routes: unplanned share is 16.6 percentage points higher than planned
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both slices must be labeled or otherwise the 16.6-point difference must be annotated.
units.temporal_anchor: optional; on a comparison of unplanned versus planned purchases, if used
units.reviewer_question: Should the video explicitly quantify the gap between unplanned and planned, or is showing the two shares enough?

units.meaning: Unplanned purchases are above the 50% majority threshold, while planned purchases are below it.
accepted_routes: a majority of purchases are unplanned
more than half of purchases are unplanned
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must make clear that the unplanned share is greater than half, e.g. by a 50% reference line or majority callout.
units.reviewer_question: Is the above-50% majority threshold an obligatory claim from 'large proportion'?

units.meaning: A gauge arc is present in the chart and is labeled 12.5%.
accepted_routes: the chart includes a 12.5% gauge arc
units.visual_evidence_rule: The gauge arc must be visible and labeled or annotated as 12.5% if this element is included.
units.temporal_anchor: not tied to the narration; optional opening or separate annotation
units.reviewer_question: Should the 12.5% gauge arc be treated as meaningful content or as a decorative/ambiguous element to ignore?

optional_valid: Unplanned is about 40% higher than planned ((58.3 - 41.7) / 41.7 = 0.398).
The two pie slices sum to 100% (58.3 + 41.7 = 100).
Use yellow for the unplanned slice and white for the planned slice if the color mapping is treated as intentional.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that store psychology caused exactly 58.3% of purchases to be unplanned; the table only provides shares.
Using 60% as the charted unplanned share because the narration says 60 while the table gives 58.3%.
Treating the 12.5% gauge arc as a third pie slice or adding it to 58.3 and 41.7.
Extrapolating to all IKEA stores, all products, or all time periods.
Claiming planned purchases are 41.7% because store psychology was absent.
notes: Table supports a 58.3% unplanned / 41.7% planned split; the 12.5% gauge arc has no defined semantic role in the intent. Review should decide whether the planned complement and derived comparisons are required or optional.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
